Both now list only what an English-only harness produces, carry a `Documentation Language` section stating the declared-locale contract, record that an existing repository never gains a locale it lacks, and the Spanish peer is faithful to the English owner again.

## 2026-08-13

- Completed `RH-W-0016` under issue #7: added lightweight immutable lifecycle records, prerequisite-safe dependencies and advancement conditions, a concise current-state projection, complete Spanish mirrors, same-work-unit documentation/session/Engram reconciliation, and generated contract coverage.
- Completed roadmap unit 2 under issue #8: default exact `.codegraph/` ignore, persistent `--no-codegraph-ignore` opt-out, manifest-driven checking, byte-preserving root `.gitignore` integration, idempotence, and changed-plan rejection.
- Required generated harnesses to reconcile applicable owning evidence before classifying repository state, report discrepancies, prefer current repository evidence over memory, verify pending or completed claims without exhaustive reading or testing, and continue organically without asking users to resolve verifiable facts.
- Added the concise adaptive harness roadmap and its complete Spanish mirror, with evidence ownership, bounded work units, verification, non-goals, and deferred integration decisions.
- Corrected current state by recording completed runtime-set widening coverage and removing only its stale pending entry.
- Added concise English and Spanish contribution guides with issue-first planning, focused branches, linked PRs, Conventional Commits, work-unit tests and docs, maintainer review, repository-specific verification, and no false claims about automation.
- Recorded the primary-source contribution-workflow comparison and the future product boundary for capability-aware contribution harnesses in consumer repositories.
- Made transport-failure remediation actionable: a generated session must now check whether an alternate credential path exists and name it, preferring provider tooling used as a single-command credential helper that changes no global configuration, and handing the exact command back to the human when the remaining path needs a secret the agent cannot supply.
- Bound generated session replies to the user's stated preferred language, otherwise to the language they are writing in, and removed the hardcoded Spanish checker report literals that forced one locale regardless of the reader.
- Made documentation language a declared choice instead of a universal assumption: a repository is English-only unless it declares more locales, so a monolingual repository no longer inherits nine Spanish files, an i18n maintenance contract, and a README selector it never asked for.
- Recorded the conversation language and the declared documentation languages in the harness manifest, validated both in the generated checker, and taught congruence checking to discover them instead of being told again.
- Separated the builder's report language, which is presentation and never enters the plan digest, from the conversation language of the built harness, which is a product choice the builder asks for.
- Fixed section comparison so the promised document chooses the vocabulary for both sides, ending a false report that named every section of a document that demonstrably still had them.
- Limited the human-owned locale check to untranslated English instead of pinning seeded template sentences that made legitimate rewriting read as drift, while the generated output keeps its complete required baseline.
- Back-filled the `doc-role` markers and refreshed the `repo-harness-help` wrappers in this repository, bringing both the builder check and the generated checker to `current`.
- Routed generated help and the preview entry points by the declared documentation locales and the conversation language instead of the report language, so a generated artifact can no longer name a guide the same render never creates, and no rendered byte depends on the report language.
